correctness.rationale: For n>=1, m>=3 and every nonempty ballot of size <=2, q=ceil(n/3), the uniform existence criterion is 2n<5q+3. If a score-optimal three-set maximizing coverage still violates JR for candidate x, each winner has score >=s(x)>=q. With >=q wholly uncovered voters, total winner scores <=2(n-q)<3(q+1), forcing a winner with s=q. Coverage-maximal exchanges and equality n=3q force a second exchange increasing coverage, contradiction. In the converse the q singleton-x voters plus n-q pair ballots distributed evenly among ab,bc,ac give all winners scores >=q+1 and a unique non-JR score optimum. The two-seat and singleton-approval boundaries are valid with their stated quantifiers.
residual_risks: Finite checks establish only their stated finite domains; infinite conclusions depend on analytic argument.
